scope.summary: Implement a hierarchical Tailor Scene Object Browser panel listing all garments, avatars, trims, and layer ordering for a workspace session with per-item visibility toggle and stable element IDs
acceptance_criteria: GET /tailor/scene returns the full scene object tree for the active workspace session: { avatars: [...], garments: [{ id, name, status, layer_order, visible, trims: [...] }] }
The frontend SceneObjectBrowser renders the tree with expand/collapse per garment and per trim, each with a visibility toggle checkbox
Toggling visibility for a garment or trim in the browser updates the viewport render without a full re-simulation
Every native tree node has a stable AccessKit author_id keyed to its entity ID plus typed Argus action/state routes for parallel-model interaction (HBR-VIS)
A model can call GET /tailor/scene to enumerate all scene entities and their layer order without a GUI session
Selecting an item in the scene browser sets the active selection context (same as clicking in the viewport)
The browser updates in real time when a garment is added, promoted, or removed during the session
Headless capture of the scene browser in populated and empty states passes the capture matrix gate (MT-244)

All operator-facing scope is implemented in src/frontend/handshake_native with native wgpu/egui, AccessKit author_id, Argus inspection/steering/capture, and no Tailor React, Tauri-command, WebView, data-testid-only, or rendered-PNG frontend path.
proof_targets: HBR-VIS: headless capture of SceneObjectBrowser with 3 garments + 2 avatars + trims passes screenshot gate
scope.risk_if_missed: Without a scene object tree, multi-garment scenes with layered garments and multiple avatars have no organized navigation surface; operators and models must use flat ID lists from the REST API, making complex layered outfit management impractical and diverging from the MD workflow where the Object Browser is the primary scene navigation tool.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

surfaces: native Tailor pane and applicable editor, viewport, browser, timeline, or status surface
argus_targets: every control and visible state introduced or changed by this MT, using stable native author_id values

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: The implementing MT must emit or project its applicable Tailor lifecycle, command, job, validation, or authority event through the shared Flight Recorder contract; pure solver kernels surface typed receipts through their owning run.
The shared internal_diagnostics substrate is supplied by WP-KERNEL-012/WP-KERNEL-016; this MT must use its open projection contract when available and must not fork a Tailor-only diagnostics runtime.
The shared Palmistry watcher is supplied by WP-KERNEL-012/WP-KERNEL-016; long-running Tailor jobs inherit bounded child-stall and survivor coverage during the retrofit.

required_changes_before_execution: Replace legacy app/src or app/src-tauri targets with the native Handshake shell and native Tailor paths.
Add canonical selection, visibility, lock, isolate, attribution, version state, filters, and large-list behavior.
Added gui_obligation, user_manual_obligation, and HBR-INT-009 tier obligations from the current MT template without removing original scope.
